name: SimplePractice vs Freed
title: SimplePractice vs Freed: EHR vs AI Scribe Comparison
description: Compare SimplePractice (practice management EHR) and Freed (AI scribe). Understand how these complementary tools serve different purposes for mental health practices.

summary.bottom_line: SimplePractice and Freed solve different problems and are complementary, not competitive. SimplePractice is a complete practice management EHR (scheduling, billing, client portal, notes). Freed is an AI scribe that generates clinical documentation from patient visits. Many practices use both: SimplePractice as their EHR and Freed to draft notes faster.

sections.heading: SimplePractice vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: SimplePractice and Freed are not competitors—they solve different problems in a clinician's workflow. SimplePractice is a comprehensive practice management EHR: it handles scheduling, client intake, insurance billing, telehealth, e-prescribing, and clinical documentation storage. Freed is an AI scribe that listens to patient sessions and generates draft clinical notes. The question isn't which to choose—it's whether to add Freed to your SimplePractice workflow to speed up documentation.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: SimplePractice costs $49/month (Starter) to $99/month (Plus) for comprehensive practice management. Freed costs $39-119/month for AI documentation. Using both would cost $88-218/month total, but provides complete practice management plus AI-assisted note writing. For clinicians spending hours on documentation, Freed's time savings may justify the additional cost on top of SimplePractice.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: SimplePractice provides: scheduling and calendar management, client portal for intake and documents, insurance billing and claims, telehealth, e-prescribing, note templates, and business reports. Freed provides: ambient listening during sessions, AI-generated SOAP/progress notes, psychiatry and therapy note formats, ICD-10 coding suggestions (Premier), and native push to SimplePractice. They address different parts of the practice workflow and integrate together.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: These tools serve different purposes—you likely need both or just SimplePractice:

recommendations.when: You need complete practice management (scheduling, billing, portal) and are comfortable writing notes manually with templates
You want complete practice management AND AI-assisted documentation to reduce note-writing time—Freed Premier pushes directly to SimplePractice
You already have a different EHR and only need AI documentation help—but Freed cannot replace SimplePractice's practice management features

faqs.a: Yes, Freed Premier ($119/month) includes native push integration with SimplePractice. Notes generated by Freed can be pushed directly into SimplePractice without copy-paste.

faqs.q: Can I use Freed instead of SimplePractice?
faqs.a: No, they serve different functions. Freed only generates clinical notes—it cannot handle scheduling, billing, client intake, telehealth, or any practice management. You need an EHR like SimplePractice regardless of whether you use Freed.

faqs.q: Is it worth paying for both SimplePractice and Freed?
faqs.a: If documentation is your biggest time sink, adding Freed ($39-119/month) to SimplePractice can save hours per week. Many clinicians find the combined cost ($88-218/month) worthwhile for the time savings on notes.

faqs.q: Does SimplePractice have AI documentation like Freed?
faqs.a: SimplePractice offers Wiley Treatment Planners for treatment planning, but does not have ambient AI listening or AI-generated session notes like Freed. For AI documentation, you would need to add Freed or a similar tool.
